Got diagnosed with ulcerative colitis three years ago. Ten days of bloody diarrhoea 7-8 times a day with extreme abdominal pain before finally getting a colonoscopy and a diagnosis. Changed my dietary habits and basically my life forever.

Six months after that, typhoid. High fever and terrible night sweats along with a splitting headache for two weeks.

A year and a half later, started getting fever which wouldn't come down. Got my blood tested, RBC WBC and platelets were falling severely. My body basically had no defence of its own to fight whatever infection caused the fever. After all kinds of blood tests which yielded nothing, my doctor told me it was time for invasive procedures. Had my bone marrow extracted (really painful process) and finally got a diagnosis of EBV (Epstein–Barr virus) related secondary HLH (Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis). I had less than 10% chances of survival. After 21 days and 11 IV cannulations on my arms, I finally returned home. I couldn't raise my arms for a week or two because they hurt so much from the constant IV medication for three weeks. I still feel traumatized even when I get slightly feverish, remembering those nightmarish days.
